_problem:
Slice 2b (fca314e) shipped a dispatch cycle that nothing ever calls: worker.ts registers boss.work(OUTBOX_DISPATCH_QUEUE) but no cron, schedule or interval ever SENDS a job to that queue, so the handler is registered and permanently idle. Verified on main at 750ca0d: zero boss.schedule() call sites, zero pg_cron (0000 installs only pgcrypto), zero setInterval — the only mentions are two aspirational comments (worker.ts:9, infra/entrypoint.sh:23). This slice is the smallest change that makes the merged lifecycle actually run.

SECOND, LARGER PROBLEM, and the reason this slice is P1 rather than trivial: pg-boss's cron path fails SILENTLY under the app_worker seat. Reading pg-boss 10.4.2 source directly rather than assuming — timekeeper.js:44-69 — start() calls manager.createQueue('__pgboss__send-it') wrapped in an EMPTY try/catch at :54-56. app_worker has no CREATE, so that call throws and is swallowed. The scheduler then work()s a queue whose partition may not exist. Worse, cron() at :141-151 does not insert into the target queue at all — it inserts into __pgboss__send-it, and the worker for THAT queue fans out to the real queue. So the entire cron path depends on an internal queue that apps/bot/src/queues.ts:18 does not list and apps/bot/src/preflight.ts:147-195 therefore never asserts a partition for. Today it exists only by accident: provision-queue.ts:24 calls boss.start() under the migration role with pg-boss's schedule:true default (attorney.js:159), which creates it as a side effect. Nothing pins that. If provisioning ever runs with schedule:false, cron dies with no error anywhere.
_decision_contract: DD-90 Q6 continues to bind and is not re-opened: the preflight fences what pg-boss's own contractor.check() does not, it runs BEFORE boss.start(), and it asserts PRESENCE of required grants — never absence of excess ones. That boundary was settled at slice 2b's MAX_ROUNDS halt (Verdict 22) and any drift back toward least-privilege attestation in this slice is an immediate HALT, not a judgement call. DD-89 Q2 also binds: pg-boss DDL authority stays in provision-queue.ts under the migration role; app_worker never creates a queue or a partition, so if this slice concludes that an object must exist, the fix is to provision it, never to grant CREATE. TDD:494 and deployment-infra:186 require every privileged cross-tenant call to write an audit row (job_id, tenant_id, actor=system, reason) — that sink already exists as job_audit_events from 0022 and the dispatch path already writes it, so this slice inherits the requirement rather than building it, and MUST NOT introduce a scheduled call path that bypasses it.
_scope_in: One module, apps/bot, TypeScript only. (1) Register a schedule for OUTBOX_DISPATCH_QUEUE so the merged dispatch cycle actually runs; cadence is a code-owned constant pinned at the design probe. (2) Close the __pgboss__send-it fence hole so a broken cron path fails LOUDLY at preflight instead of silently at runtime — the exact mechanism is the probe's job, not this manifest's. (3) Whatever preflight assertion the probe pins for the scheduler's own dependencies (the internal queue's partition, and UPDATE on pgboss.version, which timekeeper.js:129 + plans.js:375 use for the 60-second leader-election debounce). (4) Tests for the schedule registration and for the new preflight assertion, against real PostgreSQL with a real app_worker seat.
_scope_out: NO new migration — this is a hard boundary, not an oversight: everything this slice needs already exists in 0022/0023, and a migration appearing here means the slice drifted into list_due_tenant_jobs territory, which is DEFERRED to its own slice (see below) and would also collide with the parallel db-public-visibility-capacity-check slice on the `schema` invariant. NO list_due_tenant_jobs — TDD:494 names it but it does not exist on disk, and building it is a separate decision about per-tenant job claiming, not about registering one schedule. NO real projector — the injected deliver stays productionStubDeliver; touching dispatcher.ts's REQUIRED_PROJECTORS or productionStubDeliver is slice 4's scope and is forbidden here. NO change to provision-queue.ts's grant block or to queue.ts's options beyond what the probe pins for `schedule`. NO least-privilege / excess-privilege / ownership / role-attribute assertion in preflight — Verdict 22 cut that class deliberately; re-adding it is a HALT. NO enabling this schedule in any environment carrying real traffic before slice 4 lands (see the DLQ note below).
_design_probe:
Required per canonical autopilot-prompt-GENERIC v0.6.1 §0.1 — trigger (6) amends a merged core (worker.ts and preflight.ts, both from fca314e) and (8) new-mechanism choice. Before any production edit, write .autopilot/state/job-schedule-outbox-dispatch/design-probe.md pinning FIVE things and STOP for founder confirm.

(a) CADENCE AND ITS UNITS. pg-boss schedules are cron expressions, so the finest granularity is one minute. State the chosen expression, and state what happens when a cycle takes longer than the interval — pg-boss's singleton semantics for scheduled sends are the thing to read in source, not assume.

(b) THE __pgboss__send-it FENCE — the item this slice exists to get right, and the one a mechanical mirror gets wrong. The obvious move is to append '__pgboss__send-it' to QUEUES so the existing assertQueuesProvisioned covers it. Read provision-queue.ts before choosing: QUEUES also drives what provisioning CREATES, so adding pg-boss's own internal queue name there may make provisioning try to create a queue pg-boss creates itself. Determine empirically whether that is idempotent or an error, and if the two roles of QUEUES conflict, say so and propose splitting the list rather than overloading it.

(c) WHAT ELSE THE SCHEDULER NEEDS FROM THE app_worker SEAT. timekeeper.js:129 and plans.js:375-376 UPDATE pgboss.version.cron_on for leader election. provision-queue.ts:35-38 grants DML on ALL TABLES in the schema so this is probably already satisfied — verify it empirically against a real app_worker seat rather than reading the grant statement, and pin whether preflight should assert it.

(d) FAILURE MODE OF THE SWALLOWED createQueue. Given timekeeper.js:54-56 discards the error, decide what makes a broken cron path observable. Options include asserting the partition at preflight, or setting schedule:false in the runtime queue config and driving the cycle another way. State the trade-off; do not silently pick the first.

(e) WHETHER THIS SLICE SHOULD SHIP THE SCHEDULE ENABLED. Slice 2b's stub DLQs every delivery. With no producer, outbox_events is empty, so a running cron claims nothing and the DLQ flood is currently theoretical — but that changes the moment any producer lands. Pin whether the schedule registers unconditionally or behind an env flag defaulting off, and justify against DD-90's fail-closed posture.
_acceptance: JSO-1: after worker startup, a schedule row exists in pgboss.schedule for OUTBOX_DISPATCH_QUEUE with the pinned cron expression — asserted by querying the table, not by asserting the call was made.

JSO-2: THE FENCE — the row this slice exists for. With the __pgboss__send-it partition absent, preflight FAILS non-zero and names it. Without this, a broken cron path is invisible: pg-boss swallows its own createQueue error at timekeeper.js:54-56 and the scheduler silently never fires.
JSO-3: preflight still passes on a correctly provisioned cluster, and JRD-1..JRD-4 from slice 2b still hold unchanged — this slice must not weaken the DD-90 Q6 fence it is extending.

JSO-4: preflight contains ZERO role-attribute, ownership, excess-privilege or membership assertions. Assert this structurally by grepping the shipped file, not by observing that tests pass — Verdict 22 cut that class after it consumed six codex rounds, and it must not creep back.

JSO-5: the scheduler's leader-election write path works from the real app_worker seat, per whatever the probe pins in item (c) — exercised against real PostgreSQL, not asserted from the grant statement's text.

JSO-6: a scheduled send actually drives runDispatchCycle end to end — seed an outbox event, let the schedule fire (or invoke the same path the scheduler invokes), and assert the event is claimed, prepared, acked. A test that only proves the schedule row exists does NOT satisfy this row.
JSO-7: no migration is added; the tail stays 0023 and packages/db's test count is unchanged, since every test this slice adds lives in apps/bot.

JSO-8: dispatcher.ts is unmodified — REQUIRED_PROJECTORS still has exactly one entry and productionStubDeliver still returns dlq. Extending either is slice 4's scope, and dispatcher.ts:23-30 forbids extending REQUIRED_PROJECTORS under an ordinary rolling deploy until a durable versioned registry or a drain-before-enable discipline exists.
_scope_exception: Runs in PARALLEL with db-public-visibility-capacity-check (2026-07-27 owner decision). The two are disjoint by construction and this was verified rather than assumed: this slice is apps/bot only with invariants [retry-liveness]; that slice is packages/db only with invariants [schema, marketplace]. Empty file intersection, empty invariant intersection, so scripts/autopilot-scope-gate:186-193 raises neither SCOPE_COLLISION. The disjointness is CONDITIONAL ON THIS SLICE ADDING NO MIGRATION — a migration here would pull in the `schema` token and collide immediately. That is the second reason _scope_out treats it as a hard boundary rather than a preference.
_evidence_rules: Re-verify on synced main before coding, by reading rather than trusting this manifest's prose: worker.ts still has boss.work(OUTBOX_DISPATCH_QUEUE) and no boss.schedule(); QUEUES is still [OUTBOX_DISPATCH_QUEUE]; preflight's assertQueuesProvisioned still only iterates QUEUES; dispatcher.ts's REQUIRED_PROJECTORS still has exactly one entry. Read pg-boss's OWN SOURCE in node_modules for timekeeper.js and attorney.js rather than its README — the empty try/catch at timekeeper.js:54-56 and the schedule:true default at attorney.js:159 are the two facts this slice turns on, and a version bump could move either. If pg-boss's resolved version is not 10.4.2, re-derive both before proceeding. Do not invent a cadence, a fence mechanism, or an env flag in code before it is pinned in the design probe and confirmed.
_scope_reconcile: Added .env.example post-design-probe: item (e) (founder-confirmed 2026-07-27) pins a new OUTBOX_DISPATCH_SCHEDULE_ENABLED env flag defaulting off, and every other env var in this repo is documented in .env.example — leaving this one undocumented would be a real discoverability gap, not a scope-creep risk (root-level config doc, no file/invariant overlap with the parallel db-public-visibility-capacity-check slice).
